Honestly, the whole day-to-day rhythm now feels right — saving, opening, finding (including the sharper either/or searches), labelling, read-later, ordering, the preserved copies, put-away, and doing things to a batch all at once. That core loop is exactly what I pictured, and I'm really pleased with it.

Since you're asking whether it's my *complete* everyday flow, there are still a couple of things that matter to me in normal use that we haven't touched:

- **Bringing my existing bookmarks in.** Remember, the reason I wanted this app is that my bookmarks are scattered across my browser's folders right now. On day one, the first thing I'd need is to get all of those into here — otherwise I'm starting from an empty shelf and typing everything back in by hand. So importing my current browser bookmarks (keeping their names, and ideally their folders turning into labels, and when I saved them) is a real everyday need for me, not a nicety.
- **Getting a copy back out.** The flip side: I'd want to be able to export my whole collection to a file now and then, both for peace of mind and so I'm never locked in. Given how much I'm trusting this app to hold, being able to take my own copy matters.

Two smaller ones, lower priority:

- **Saving a search I use a lot.** I just built up some fairly detailed searches; it'd be handy to save one I return to often — a particular label-plus-words combination — so I can pull it up again with one click instead of rebuilding it each time.
- **A few comfort settings.** Little personal-preference things like how many bookmarks show at once, the text size, and which order my list defaults to.

None of that takes away from what you've shown — the core is solid. I'd just want the import and export especially rounded in before I'd call it my truly complete everyday setup. Can we work through those? (And notes, plus searching them, still happily parked for later as we agreed.)
